GlobalPolicy.module-level-focus: Prefer compile checks, replay round-trips, and narrow scenario validation near the changed Vast surface.
GlobalPolicy.wave-level-focus: Validate only the merged gameplay, UI, serialization, and bot surfaces touched by the current execution wave.
GlobalPolicy.phase-level-focus: Run broader browser and host confidence checks before marking a large Vast phase complete.
GlobalPolicy.redaction: Never log secrets from URL/server parameters and avoid leaking hidden-information state when adding new gameplay logs.

VF-START-4P.NAME: Start four-player Vast game
VF-START-4P.scenario: The browser runtime starts a standard four-player game and reaches a playable initial board.
VF-START-4P.expected-outcome: Assets load, faction validation passes, and the initial state renders without runtime failure.

VF-RESOLVE-TURN.NAME: Resolve legal action correctly
VF-RESOLVE-TURN.scenario: A human or bot performs a legal faction action and the next game state remains rules-correct.
VF-RESOLVE-TURN.expected-outcome: Only legal actions resolve, hidden information stays consistent, and victory progress remains valid.

VF-SERIALIZE-ROUNDTRIP.NAME: Round-trip externalized actions
VF-SERIALIZE-ROUNDTRIP.scenario: An external action is written to string form, parsed back, and remains semantically equivalent.
VF-SERIALIZE-ROUNDTRIP.expected-outcome: Replay/debugging evidence stays trustworthy and does not drift between write and parse steps.

VF-BOT-LEGALITY.NAME: Bot selects only legal actions
VF-BOT-LEGALITY.scenario: A bot-controlled faction advances the game through the same legal action surface as a human player.
VF-BOT-LEGALITY.expected-outcome: Simulation progresses without illegal-action divergence or engine crashes.

required-signals.trace-sequence: collect legal actions -> evaluate -> choose -> apply through game engine

VF-THIEF-5P.NAME: Enable five-player Thief support
VF-THIEF-5P.scenario: A five-player setup including Thief starts successfully and Thief-specific actions behave according to `rules/thief.xml`.
VF-THIEF-5P.expected-outcome: Five-player validation succeeds, Thief can act legally, and existing four-player flows still work.

required-signals.trace-sequence: read thief rules -> expand setup validation -> render fifth faction -> serialize and simulate actions

module-checks.check-1: Manual document review to map changed mechanics to the relevant XML rule sections before implementation.

scenarios.scenario-1: Every modified gameplay rule has an explicit XML reference in the current work packet or review notes.

required-trace-assertions.assertion-1: Mechanic changes should not proceed without identifying the matching rules document.

V-M-VAST-RULES.wave-follow-up: Update downstream verification entries when a new rules area becomes in scope.
V-M-VAST-RULES.phase-follow-up: Perform a targeted rules-versus-code review for all changed factions.

module-checks.check-3: After large `performInternal` splits (`performInternalPart2`), build with `HRF_VAST_SIM=1`, then on Node: `VAST_SIM_ITERATIONS=1` (optionally `VAST_SIM_SKIP_ROUNDTRIP=1` for a faster smoke) using `hrf-fastopt.js`.

scenarios.scenario-1: Legal actions update the game state correctly for supported factions.
scenarios.scenario-2: Invalid setup or illegal action assumptions are rejected before corrupting state.

required-trace-assertions.assertion-1: State transitions must remain the sole authority for rules enforcement regardless of UI or bot caller.

V-M-VAST-GAME.wave-follow-up: Run focused scenario checks for any faction or mechanic touched by the wave.
V-M-VAST-GAME.phase-follow-up: Complete a broader gameplay regression pass across supported factions.

module-checks.check-1: Run host-side round-trip scenarios that write, parse, and compare external actions.

scenarios.scenario-1: Stable external actions round-trip without semantic drift.
scenarios.scenario-2: Unexpected action shapes produce diagnosable failures rather than silent corruption.

required-trace-assertions.assertion-1: Serialization changes must be checked against replay/debug workflows, not only compile success.

V-M-VAST-SERIALIZE.wave-follow-up: Re-run any scenario packs affected by changed action shapes.
V-M-VAST-SERIALIZE.phase-follow-up: Capture representative replay samples for the changed mechanics.

module-checks.check-1: Run host-side simulations and confirm bots only choose legal actions.

scenarios.scenario-1: Current bots can advance supported factions through complete games without engine errors.
scenarios.scenario-2: Bot scoring changes do not bypass legal action filtering.

required-trace-assertions.assertion-1: Any future stronger AI must still consume a legal-action boundary rather than raw UI state.

V-M-VAST-BOT.wave-follow-up: Check result distributions and obvious pathological choices after bot changes.
V-M-VAST-BOT.phase-follow-up: Establish stronger benchmarking once the AI integration path is defined.

module-checks.check-2: Browser startup smoke after changing faction validation or asset registration.

scenarios.scenario-1: Supported faction combinations validate and create the correct game/UI entry points.
scenarios.scenario-2: Unsupported combinations fail explicitly instead of entering broken runtime states.

required-trace-assertions.assertion-1: Changing player-count constraints must be accompanied by downstream UI and game-engine verification.

V-M-VAST-META.wave-follow-up: Re-run all affected startup permutations after validation logic changes.
V-M-VAST-META.phase-follow-up: Review supported faction matrix before marking a setup-related phase complete.

scenarios.scenario-1: The map, factions, overlays, and click targets render correctly for supported states.
scenarios.scenario-2: Hidden information is not leaked by rendering or hover behavior.

required-trace-assertions.assertion-1: UI-only changes must still be validated against actual legal-action and hidden-information rules.

V-M-VAST-UI.wave-follow-up: Manually validate the exact interaction surface touched by the wave.
V-M-VAST-UI.phase-follow-up: Complete a browser regression pass for startup, navigation, and end-to-end gameplay checkpoints.

module-checks.check-1: Run host-side simulation batches after bot or serialization changes.

scenarios.scenario-1: Simulation batches complete and emit usable result summaries.
scenarios.scenario-2: Divergent games emit actionable failure artifacts rather than silent stops.

required-trace-assertions.assertion-1: Host validation should remain capable of exercising the same action/serialization path as live gameplay.

V-M-VAST-HOST.wave-follow-up: Re-run simulations whenever legal-action generation or parsing changes.
V-M-VAST-HOST.phase-follow-up: Use host evidence as one input into AI-readiness reviews.

scenarios.scenario-1: The browser app loads resources and hands control to the Vast UI successfully.
scenarios.scenario-2: Resource or route issues fail clearly instead of partially loading a broken runtime.

required-trace-assertions.assertion-1: Runtime bootstrap checks must be rerun whenever browser-launch files are edited for Vast work.

V-M-HRF-WEB-RUNTIME.wave-follow-up: Smoke the browser path after changing any launch-critical file.
V-M-HRF-WEB-RUNTIME.phase-follow-up: Use startup verification as a gate for any phase that touches browser execution.

module-checks.check-3: Run a five-player startup and focused Thief scenario pass.
module-checks.check-4: Run host-side replay/simulation checks that include Thief actions.
module-checks.check-5: Before continuing implementation, rerun `sbt compile` because the last post-filter compile was interrupted after documenting the JVM limit workaround.

scenarios.scenario-1: A five-player setup including Thief starts successfully, mixes Vault tiles from `setup.has(Thief)`, and exposes only legal Thief actions.
scenarios.scenario-2: Thief setup creates runtime state for Movement, Stealth, Thievery, action cubes, Entrance position, carried loot, and stashed loot.
scenarios.scenario-3: Thief core turn flow supports stat assignment, movement, dark-tile peek/reveal, end-turn cleanup, and death basics according to `rules/thief.xml`.
scenarios.scenario-4: Thief Loot, Pick Lock, Vault, stash, Dragon Gem, treasure shortage, and six-stash victory behavior match `rules/thief.xml`.
scenarios.scenario-5: Pickpocket, Backstab, Stealth targeting, target-once-per-turn, and Unnatural Evasion integrate with Knight, Goblins, Dragon, and Cave interactions.
scenarios.scenario-6: Thief interactions serialize, replay, render, and simulate through host/bot paths correctly.
scenarios.scenario-7: Existing four-player setups continue to work unchanged after Thief support lands.
scenarios.scenario-8: Additional Thief/cross-faction action handlers must not be added directly to `Game.performInternal`; first extract smaller dispatch helpers to avoid JVM `Method too large`.

required-trace-assertions.assertion-1: Five-player enablement must prove both new Thief behavior and non-regression of current four-player flows.
required-trace-assertions.assertion-2: Each implemented Thief mechanic must cite the matching `rules/thief.xml` section in work notes or code review notes.
required-trace-assertions.assertion-3: Host evidence at the checkpoint reached `[VastThief][enable]`, `[VastThief][turn]`, and `[VastThief][loot]`; remaining failures were cross-faction targeting gaps, not initial Thief setup failure.
required-trace-assertions.assertion-4: Temporary filters around Goblins Hex and Cave Soporific Spores prevent unimplemented Thief target handlers until cross-faction extraction is complete.
required-trace-assertions.assertion-5: Refactor wave 1 preserves action class names and delegates setup/Thief bodies through `GameSetupSupport` and `GameThiefSupport` without adding new behavior.

V-M-VAST-THIEF-SUPPORT.wave-follow-up: Re-run setup, UI, serialization, and simulation checks for all touched surfaces after each Thief wave.
V-M-VAST-THIEF-SUPPORT.phase-follow-up: Do not mark Thief support complete until both five-player and four-player evidence are green.

Gate-Phase-1.goal: The current Vast architecture is documented with clear references from rules to core engine surfaces.

required-evidence.evidence-1: Core modules and rule references are anchored and navigable.

Gate-Phase-2.goal: Browser startup and gameplay interaction surfaces are stable enough for iterative work.

required-evidence.evidence-1: Startup and one or more critical gameplay scenarios work in the browser.

Gate-Phase-3.goal: Bot and host validation loops are trustworthy enough to support future AI work.

commands.command-1: Run host-side simulation batches for supported factions.

required-evidence.evidence-1: Bots choose only legal actions and simulations produce useful evidence.

Gate-Phase-4.goal: Thief is enabled as the fifth player with verified non-regression of the current game.

commands.command-3: Run a five-player Thief startup and gameplay validation pass.

required-evidence.evidence-2: Thief-specific mechanics match `rules/thief.xml` for the implemented scenarios.
